daily.full:
Consensus

The clearest common bullish name today was $LITE: 4 accounts explicitly bullish across 23 related posts. @kevinxu said he hopes someone dreamed of photonics — a full position in calls would be legendary. Post @aleabitoreddit reported that $MRVL is in the final stage of acquiring $LITE, aiming to ease supply bottlenecks through laser vertical integration; if it goes through, other laser makers could be re-rated. Post @StockSavvyShay highlighted $MRVL profit growing nearly 10x to about $14B by FY2029, hoping to benefit as hyperscalers keep raising AI spend.

Common bearish

$INTC had 3 bearish accounts. @hkuppy said don't forget 2000 — the semiconductor mania ended when Intel blew up; shares sank after hours on a sharply lower Q4 guide (adjusted EPS $0.25 vs $0.43 expected). Post @munster_gene said the main issue is PC demand slowing on high memory costs, and it should not be extrapolated to $NVDA.

Split

$GOOGL was the most-mentioned ticker today (66 mentions), with clearly divided views. @Mr_Derivatives noted that despite a 10% drop, every major analyst still has big targets of $375–425, 30–47% above the current price — buy the dip? Post Meanwhile @TheTranscript_ reported Alphabet's CEO saying AI tools help engineers ship 35% more code with 30% fewer bugs. Post Some see strong fundamentals; others worry about after-hours weakness dragging the market.

Also worth noting

Small caps in $IWM were relatively strong; @Mr_Derivatives said it almost touched $283 after hours after a decent rebound over the past week. Post $CVNA beat estimates with retail units +39% to a record, up 8% after hours; @michaelsikand mentioned an $1.8B hedge fund manager with 80% of capital long. Post On $MU, one account sees a possible $1,700 within 18 months, saying bears will be proven wrong again as free-cash-flow estimates have been raised sharply.

daily.brief: Over the past ~27 hours, 58 accounts posted 320 related items. Common bearish is led by $RDDT (10 accounts) and $INTC (9 accounts). Common bullish is led by $NVDA (4 accounts). Biggest splits are on $AMZN (5 long / 2 short) and $SNDK (3/4) after earnings.
daily.full:
Consensus

Clearest common bullish today is $NVDA, with 4 accounts long and 13 related posts. @Beth_Kindig estimates Nvidia ACIE revenue growth may outpace hyperscalers (138.5% vs 101.2%) and could catch up in about five to six quarters. post @Jason said he bought some $GOOG and $NVDA, citing strong leadership and products. post @StockSavvyShay noted reports that $NVDA is in talks to provide over $5B of credit support for a 460MW Nscale data center backed by a $45B $ANT compute contract. post On rotation, @KeithMcCullough said Hedgeye put its highest equity allocation into healthcare $XLV, with the community also re-adding staples $XLP.

Common Bearish

$RDDT has 10 bearish accounts, the densest common short today, with 24 related posts. @ripster47 called it a major disappointment after daily active users missed, saying longs were covered around $135 and framing a 100 PSYCH short setup. post @StockSavvyShay listed $RDDT among October growth-stock drawdowns (about -41%). post $INTC has 9 bearish accounts and 48 posts: @TrendSpider said it was down about 30% from the prior close, the worst drop in the company's 55-year history; @garyblack00 pointed to soft PC demand outlook and guidance as accelerating tech outflows. post post Several also flagged $NOW wiping out three months of gains and breaking the 200-day average.

Divergence

$AMZN is among the most-mentioned names, with 5 bullish and 2 bearish accounts and 66 posts. @munster_gene argued AWS growth supports a new narrative, with AWS about 25% of sales today and maybe at least half of revenue in five years; @ChrisCamillo said he aggressively added $AMZN while de-levering elsewhere, viewing the market as too dangerous for short-term over-trading; @saxena_puru noted the post-print drop but said AI buildout is not slowing, with Alphabet maintaining $195-205B 2026 capex guidance. post post post $SNDK is similarly split (3 long / 4 short): some cite the Sandisk CEO saying AI infrastructure customers underestimated NAND demand, while others still list it among post-earnings tech declines.

Other Notable

@RedDogT3 noted that at least $TSLA offers a layered system to navigate, holding $387-$388 to add and manage. post @OptionsMike is watching the $SPY 748.80 level. On the drone/defense theme, @ripster47 and @TrendSpider mentioned names like $ONDS warming up. Overall, post-earnings stock differentiation exceeds any single index narrative.

weekly.brief: Over the past 7 days, 1,837 posts from 123 accounts. Common bullish was concentrated in $SKHY and $SOFI (7 accounts each); common bearish was led by $BA. The biggest splits were $SPY and $MU.
weekly.full:
Consensus

The most concentrated common bullish names this week were $SKHY and $SOFI, with 7 bullish accounts each. @ripster47 advised struggling traders to log repeatable setups; in earnings season $SKHY was a stress-free 4R trade today, just keep trailing the stop. Post @ThetaWarrior, citing an earlier alert, said sweepers took profits of over $4M in total. On $SOFI, @Jake__Wujastyk pointed to a solid recovery in the monthly candle, and @RedDogT3 said a post-earnings pattern like yesterday's is rare lately, with a plan to swing long using the gap pivot as reference.

Common bearish

$BA had 4 bearish accounts. @Mr_Derivatives said BA fell 10% today to a 1.5-year low. Post Other bearish calls included $ENPH, down roughly 14–20% after missing estimates.

Split

$SPY and $MU were clearly split. $MU had 14 bullish and 2 bearish accounts, with one seeing $1,700 within 18 months. $TSLA and the semiconductor ETF $SMH also drew bullish voices, but the broader market reacted unevenly after the FOMC.

Also worth noting

Semiconductor ETF investors were actively buying the dip across $SMH, $SOXL and $DRAM. The $LITE photonics theme carried into the weekly view, in line with the daily consensus.

monthly.brief: Over the past 28 days, 6,083 posts from 155 accounts. Common bullish was led by $SOFI and $LITE; common bearish stayed concentrated in $BA. The biggest splits were $CRWV (6 bullish vs 24 bearish) and $SPY.
monthly.full:
Consensus

Over the past month the most concentrated common bullish names were $SOFI (8 accounts) and $LITE (5 accounts). Photonics and fintech themes held up on the longer time frame. $MSTR, $RSP and $AEHR also had 5 bullish accounts each.

Common bearish

$BA kept 4 bearish accounts, consistent with the weekly view. Other common bearish names included $TMUS, $SBUX and $ENPH.

Split

$CRWV was the most extreme split: 6 bullish accounts but 24 bearish. @KeithMcCullough said the AI bubble has started to pop, beginning with the neoclouds; CoreWeave closed at $54.24 on Oct 23, well off its 52-week high. Post On the other side, one account noted that even $GOOGL can't bring capacity online fast enough to meet demand, which helps names like $CRWV. $TSLA had 22 bullish and 3 bearish accounts; $SPY was 12 bullish vs 13 bearish.

Also worth noting

Overall, AI-related splits (especially neoclouds and semiconductors) were most visible on the monthly view, while traditional defensive and consumer names drew few common bullish calls.

In the monthly frame, AI-related names (especially new cloud) show the widest divergence, while consumer finance, payments, and some defensive names more often appear on the common bullish side. Accounts mention a $MU $1,700 target over the next 18 months.
